subject: Intermittent large-packet drops after private cutover - NordiCare (MTU/SNAT)
messages:
From: Erik Lindström <erik.lindstrom@nordichealth.se>
To: ava.chen@redwood.ai
Cc: nordichealth-netops@support.nordichealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 08:23:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private cutover - some traffic failing (large packets)

Hi Ava,

We flipped the private cutover to Redwood Private in our Stockholm colo at 07:45 local and are seeing a subset of application traffic fail intermittently. Symptoms:
- Certain API calls time out (client-side logs show TCP retransmits).
- Bulk file uploads (SFTP/HTTPS) fail around ~1400-1450 byte payloads. Smaller payloads OK.
- Traceroutes from our app tier to Redwood frontends show PMTU blackhole behavior — path MTU ~1500 but packets above ~1420 are dropped.

I've attached a small pcap and a path-trace (pcap excerpt) to this message. We're also seeing a handful of flows that return via a different NAT IP (asymmetric return path) which breaks session pinning on our firewall.

Can Redwood help triage? We need this resolved urgently — it's affecting production syncs with our EHR queues.

Thanks,
Erik
Network Engineer, NordicHealth
[Attachment: nordichealth-pcap-20260618-trace1.txt (text/plain)]

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Erik Lindström <erik.lindstrom@nordichealth.se>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 08:45:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private cutover - some traffic failing (large packets)

Hi Erik — thanks for the quick report and the pcap. Sorry you're seeing this after the cutover.

Looping in Dev (network infra) and Marissa (customer success) — we'll triage immediately. Initial hypotheses from the symptoms:
- MTU / MSS clamping mismatch at the hybrid gateway or an intermediate device (causes fragmentation/blackhole)
- SNAT asymmetry because of path selection differences between front-door and egress routers
- Security group / firewall session timeouts due to different source IPs on return path

Immediate requests:
- Erik: can you paste the output of "ip route get <redwood-frontdoor-ip>" from one of the app hosts, and the exact tcpdump filter you used for the pcap?
- Dev/Network: can you check the hybrid gateway's PMTU discovery logs and any egress SNAT map changes around 07:40-08:00 UTC?

We have a short call available at 09:00 UTC if that's possible — Marissa, can you join and coordinate?

I'll collect logs and a small verification playbook to walk through canary rollbacks if needed.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — private@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: ava.chen@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: erik.lindstrom@nordichealth.se
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:10:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private cutover - some traffic failing (large packets)

Thanks Erik/Ava — quick triage notes from the infra side after a first pass:

What I checked (07:30–08:50 UTC window):
- Hybrid gateway (staging-stk01): no kernel dmesg MTU clamping logs, but we do see ICMP fragmentation-needed messages being rate-limited (possible intermediate device dropping ICMP).
- SNAT pool: we have two egress NAT IPs configured for NordiCare; routing changes during cutover show some flows preferred a different next-hop (path selection change), explaining asymmetric return.
- Security groups: session nat mapping exists but some return packets hit a different NAT IP so pinning breaks on their firewall appliance.

Action plan (short):
1) Ask customer to temporarily enable MSS clamping on their app hosts to 1360 to mitigate while we locate the blackhole. Command: iptables --append FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu (or set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1).
2) We'll force symmetric egress for App -> Redwood frontdoor flows by pinning the SNAT mapping for affected subnets and BGP pref telemetry to prefer the same NAT IP for the return path.
3) Collect additional tcpdumps on both sides for the affected five flows (already flagged in the pcap).

Marissa: I'll open a temporary rollback flag if symmetric NAT cannot be achieved quickly (we can revert to previous peering adjacency for the affected VLANs).

Erik: can you confirm you can run MSS clamping and grab an ip route get and a tcpdump using the filter "host <frontdoor-ip> and tcp"? Also send a copy of the firewall's SNAT/pinning timeouts if available.

- Dev

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: dev.patel@redwood.ai, ava.chen@redwood.ai
Cc: erik.lindstrom@nordichealth.se

Thanks Dev. Erik — we're prioritizing this. A few coordination notes:

- I've scheduled a 09:00 UTC troubleshooting bridge and bumped it to 09:10 to let Dev collect logs; join link: https://meet.redwood.com/infra-escalation-0900
- I'll coordinate a canary rollback window for 09:35 UTC if the mitigation doesn't reduce failures by 09:30.
- CS asks the customer to confirm business impact window (what jobs fail, are retries happening?) — this helps size the rollback risk.

Erik: let us know whether the MSS-clamp test helped and paste any firewall logs you can share. We'll try the SNAT pinning change from the Redwood side first to avoid a full rollback.

-Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Erik Lindström <erik.lindstrom@nordichealth.se>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private cutover - some traffic failing (large packets)

Erik — quick update and next steps after the bridge:

What we did during the call:
- Customer ran MSS clamp to 1360 on two app hosts; their large uploads that previously failed now succeed in the canary run.
- Dev pinned SNAT for the /28 app subnet to NAT IP 203.0.113.45 and confirmed symmetric return for test flows.
- We captured tcpdumps on customer side and our hybrid gateway; preliminary comparison shows ICMP frag-needed being dropped by a middlebox inside the colo (ticket opened with colo ops).

Immediate mitigation:
- Keep MSS clamp enabled for production app hosts (can be rolled via config management).
- We're rolling a config to pin SNAT for the affected subnet for the next 6 hours to avoid asymmetric pinning while colo Ops investigates the intermediate device.
- CS will monitor error rates; if we see no improvement by 13:00 UTC we'll execute the rollback plan.

Attached: checklist we used and a sanitized excerpt of the tcpdump pairs. Also linking the JIRA we filed for tracking.

Next asks for NordicHealth:
- Please confirm when MSS-clamp is applied across the full app fleet and share firewall SNAT timeout values if you can (helps tune our pinning TTL).
- If colo Ops can provide the middlebox config/ACLs that might be dropping ICMP frag-needed, that would be ideal.

Erik — apologies for the disruption and thanks for the fast collaboration. We'll continue monitoring and will keep you updated in-channel.

Best,
Ava Chen
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
